Here's the corrected code and the solution to your problem:

**Problem Statement:**

Write a Java program that takes an HTML string as input and parses it using Jsoup.

**Solution:**

```java
import org.jsoup.Jsoup;
import org.jsoup.nodes.Document;

public class Main {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String html = "<html><head></head><body>Hello</body></html>";
        Document doc = Jsoup.parse(html);
        System.out.println(doc.body().text());
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**

*   We import the required classes from Jsoup library.
*   In the `main` method, we define an HTML string and parse it using `Jsoup.parse`.
*   The `doc` object now contains the parsed HTML document.
*   Finally, we print the text content of the parsed HTML document using `doc.body().text()`.

**Example Use Case:**

You can use this code to parse any HTML string that you want. Simply replace the input string with your own HTML content and run the program.

Remember to include the Jsoup library in your project's classpath for this code to work. You can do this by including the following dependency in your `pom.xml` file (if you're using Maven):

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.jsoup</groupId>
    <artifactId>jsoup</artifactId>
    <version>1.15.3</version>
</dependency>
```

Or by including it directly in your project's build path.

**Tips and Variations:**

*   To parse a URL as HTML, you can pass the URL to `Jsoup.parse()`:

    ```java
Document doc = Jsoup.connect("http://www.example.com").get();
```
